article_title: Methodologies for Improving the Quality of AI Tutoring in K-12 Education
citation: Udeshi, T., Khazenzon, A., Khan, K., Breen, N., Corwin, R., DiGiano, C., Weatherholtz, K., Zaluski, M. (2026). Methodologies for Improving the Quality of AI Tutoring in K-12 Education. https://sites.google.com/khanacademy.org/aied2026supplementalmaterial/home
title: Khanmigo AI Component workflow architecture with declarative overrides
description: Each Khanmigo feature is a chat-based workflow with its own system prompt, guardrails, and configurable steps. The lowest-level building block is the AI Component: "a simple, generic function that we expect to have variable output, usually from an LLM call." Components are called through a single entry point providing standardized logging, offline-evaluation compatibility, and declarative dot-notation overrides of inputs such as prompt variables and model attributes. Because the workflow entry point is itself an AI Component, experiments can add, remove, or replace whole workflow steps.
requirements: A single entry point that automatically provides standardized logging and tracing, compatibility with offline evaluation tooling, and declarative input overrides
constraints: The platform is primarily written in Go with a small Python service supporting a Math Agent that runs student math in a sandbox with NumPy and SymPy
target_learners: K-12 students using Khanmigo Exercise and Tutor Me features
target_learning_goals: AI tutoring quality across math, science, essay writing, and humanities tutoring requests
examples: The Exercise chat workflow moderates student input, runs a Python Math Agent to identify math errors, and injects the Math Agent result as context before responding
key_sources: Udeshi, T., Khazenzon, A., Khan, K., Breen, N., Corwin, R., DiGiano, C., Weatherholtz, K., Zaluski, M. (2026). Methodologies for Improving the Quality of AI Tutoring in K-12 Education. https://sites.google.com/khanacademy.org/aied2026supplementalmaterial/home

article_title: Methodologies for Improving the Quality of AI Tutoring in K-12 Education
citation: Udeshi, T., Khazenzon, A., Khan, K., Breen, N., Corwin, R., DiGiano, C., Weatherholtz, K., Zaluski, M. (2026). Methodologies for Improving the Quality of AI Tutoring in K-12 Education. https://sites.google.com/khanacademy.org/aied2026supplementalmaterial/home
title: Offline evaluation datasets and calibrated LLM judges for tutoring behaviors
description: The team maintains targeted offline datasets sampled from production completions, including an answer-giveaway dataset where "The final dataset consists of 63 data points" and a Tutor Me input-classification dataset where "the dataset consisted of 794 data points." LLM judges calibrated against human experts measure cognitive engagement, math errors, and answer giveaway; the engagement judge shows "an F1 score of 0.83, Matthews Correlation Coefficient of 0.75, false positive rate of 0.08, and false negative rate of 0.17."
requirements: Datasets must be stripped of PII and kept up to date as user behavior drifts; judge prompts are published as supplemental material
constraints: Offline evaluations currently evaluate only a single turn of a model; user simulation has been explored only in limited contexts
target_learning_goals: Measuring answer giveaway, request classification, math accuracy, and cognitive engagement in tutoring conversations
examples: The giveaway dataset was built by sampling production completions, running an LLM judge, filtering to giveaway cases, and filtering to cases where a human expert agreed with the judge label
key_sources: Udeshi, T., Khazenzon, A., Khan, K., Breen, N., Corwin, R., DiGiano, C., Weatherholtz, K., Zaluski, M. (2026). Methodologies for Improving the Quality of AI Tutoring in K-12 Education. https://sites.google.com/khanacademy.org/aied2026supplementalmaterial/home

article_title: Khan Academy as Supplemental Instruction: A Controlled Study of a Computer-Based Mathematics Intervention
citation: Daniel P. Kelly and Teomara Rutherford. (2017). Khan Academy as Supplemental Instruction: A Controlled Study of a Computer-Based Mathematics Intervention. International Review of Research in Open and Distributed Learning, 18(4). https://www.irrodl.org
title: Khan Academy as a computer-based supplemental mathematics intervention
description: Khan Academy is a large, free open educational resource offering video-based lectures paired with problems for students to solve, with points and badges that "serve to provide positive reinforcement and encouragement." In this study it was used by seventh graders for a minimum of 30 minutes per class over four weeks as a self-paced, self-directed supplement, with students free to choose topics, simulating typical at-home use. The platform internally tracks metrics including minutes spent, points attained, and topics mastered.
requirements: Requires student access to the platform and time allocated within or alongside class; in this study time was tracked by the classroom teacher and used as a daily participation grade
constraints: The study examined only use as it might occur at home without a teacher's guidance or knowledge; students were not assigned specific topics
target_learning_goals: mathematics achievement on standardized end-of-grade assessment content
examples: Treatment students worked with Khan Academy a minimum of 30 minutes per class over a four-week period without assigned topics
key_sources: Daniel P. Kelly and Teomara Rutherford. (2017). Khan Academy as Supplemental Instruction: A Controlled Study of a Computer-Based Mathematics Intervention. International Review of Research in Open and Distributed Learning, 18(4). https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1146230

citation: Стрюк А.М., Семеріков С.О. (2012). МОДЕЛІ КОМБІНОВАНОГО НАВЧАННЯ. https://www.google.com/search?q=%22Моделі+комбінованого+навчання%22+Стрюк+Семеріков
title: Вісім вимог Б. Хана до розробки моделі комбінованого навчання
description: Стаття наводить перелік вимог, які, «на думку Б. Хана, вимагає урахування вимог: педагогічних, технологічних, інституційних, етичних, управлінських, ресурсних, інтерфейсних та оцінювальних» при розробці моделі комбінованого навчання. Цей перелік слугує в статті одним із орієнтирів для аналізу існуючих моделей та обґрунтування нової організаційної моделі, що інтегрує синхронні та асинхронні комунікаційні технології, формальне та неформальне навчання, друковані та електронні матеріали.
requirements: урахування педагогічних, технологічних, інституційних, етичних, управлінських, ресурсних, інтерфейсних та оцінювальних вимог
target_learning_goals: проєктування та оцінювання моделей комбінованого навчання
examples: перелік використано як рамку для критики та розробки моделей у статті

article_title: Using Mathcasts to Facilitate Student Comprehension of Physical Applications of Math Concepts
citation: Colleen Lanz Countryman and Hong Wang, North Carolina State University, Raleigh, NC. (2014). Using Mathcasts to Facilitate Student Comprehension of Physical Applications of Math Concepts. https://www.youtube.com/user/LearnMathandPhysics
title: Khan-Academy-style mathcast design: short, personal videos with hand-sketching, talking head, and physical demonstrations
description: The article describes a reusable video design pattern for out-of-class mathematics review: videos kept "short and personal", modeled after Khan Academy tutorials, without PowerPoint slides, using only typewritten problem statements, interspersed "talking head" segments and demonstrations with physical objects where appropriate, with the instructor speaking quickly and with enthusiasm. Hand-sketching and handwriting were chosen because they "have both been shown to increase student engagement over computer-rendered graphics and text".
requirements: Instructor able to hand-sketch and narrate; videos kept short and personal rather than slide-based lectures
target_learners: undergraduate physics students in an electricity and magnetism course
target_learning_goals: connect prior mathematics concepts (dot/cross products, limits of integration, solving systems of equations) to current physics concepts (work/torque, electric fields, Kirchhoff's Laws)
examples: Six videos produced over the semester used a drawing program blackboard, screen recording, and physical-object demonstrations such as for the right hand rule.
key_sources: Colleen Lanz Countryman and Hong Wang, North Carolina State University, Raleigh, NC. (2014). Using Mathcasts to Facilitate Student Comprehension of Physical Applications of Math Concepts. https://www.youtube.com/user/LearnMathandPhysics

article_title: Quantum education in the frontier city of Kharkiv
citation: Pylyp Kuznietsov, Igor Girka, Igor Kyryllin, Andrii Sotnikov. (2024). Quantum education in the frontier city of Kharkiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14302
title: Kharkiv quantum education initiatives of 2023-2024: qUA workgroup, US-Ukraine Quantum Forum, and Kharkiv Quantum Seminar series
description: Three linked initiatives emerged in 2023 to sustain and internationalize quantum education and research at SPT. In May 2023 a voluntary quantum workgroup (qUA) of the Ukrainian Physical Society was formed by representatives of Kharkiv, Kyiv, Lviv, and Donetsk to promote Ukrainian quantum scientists within the EU Quantum Flagship landscape. The US-Ukraine Quantum Forum (August 28-31, 2023) brought together 32 speakers over four days with more than 50 attending scientists and students. Since October 2023 the regular virtual Kharkiv Quantum Seminar series features mid-career and diaspora speakers plus world-leading invited specialists. The authors write that "we organized the Kharkiv Quantum Seminar series, which are held on a regular basis in the virtual format since October 2023."
requirements: Virtual formats and international partner engagement; the forum's Ukrainian speakers were supported by honoraria from an Office of Naval Research Global grant
constraints: Ukrainian researchers under travel restrictions (notably the male category) could participate mainly through virtual events
target_learners: Ukrainian quantum physics researchers and students, including those under travel restrictions
target_learning_goals: connection to the international quantum research community, awareness of research and educational initiatives, seminars and calls
examples: SPT students won first prize at the QHack UA Bootcamp 2024 winter school and first prize in the "A Matter of Taste" challenge at international QHack 2024
key_sources: Pylyp Kuznietsov, Igor Girka, Igor Kyryllin, Andrii Sotnikov. (2024). Quantum education in the frontier city of Kharkiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14302

article_title: Khelte Khelte Shikhi: A Proposed HCI Framework for Gamified Interactive Learning with Minecraft in Bangladeshi Education Systems
citation: Mohd Ruhul Ameen, Akif Islam, Momen Khandokar Ope. (2025). Khelte Khelte Shikhi: A Proposed HCI Framework for Gamified Interactive Learning with Minecraft in Bangladeshi Education Systems. https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18385
title: A four-layer framework for Minecraft-based learning integrating infrastructure, curriculum, interaction, and institutional support
description: The article proposes a system architecture of "four interdependent layers" that jointly integrate infrastructure, pedagogy, content, and institutional support. The Institutional & Training Layer handles "Policy alignment, teacher professional development, partnerships, open licensing"; the Interaction & Pedagogy Layer covers inclusive UI/UX, adaptive tutorials, and accessibility tools; the Content & Curriculum Layer provides culturally grounded, curriculum-mapped bilingual worlds; and the Infrastructure Layer handles tiered deployment, hardware provisioning, power, and offline-ready distribution. The authors state each layer "works independently but they are stronger when combined."
requirements: Schools can implement what works for their situation without needing everything at once
constraints: Presented as a design-oriented conceptual framework rather than a field deployment; no empirical classroom trials yet
target_learners: Students in Bangladeshi government primary and secondary schools, grades 3-12, including first-time computer users
target_learning_goals: Curriculum-aligned learning in science, math, social studies, and languages
examples: Table II assigns responsibilities to each layer, from tiered deployment and solar power in the Infrastructure Layer to open licensing in the Institutional & Training Layer
key_sources: Mohd Ruhul Ameen, Akif Islam, Momen Khandokar Ope. (2025). Khelte Khelte Shikhi: A Proposed HCI Framework for Gamified Interactive Learning with Minecraft in Bangladeshi Education Systems. https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18385

article_title: Simulation-based skills training in non-performing orthopedic surgeons: skills acquisition, motivation, and flow during the COVID-19 pandemic.
citation: Hedman Leif Rune, Felländer-Tsai Li. (2020). Simulation-based skills training in non-performing orthopedic surgeons: skills acquisition, motivation, and flow during the COVID-19 pandemic. Acta Orthopaedica. https://doi.org/10.1080/17453674.2020.1781413
title: Khamis et al. stepwise model integrating curriculum development and simulation design principles
description: The article presents the model of Khamis et al. (2016) as a curriculum-design resource for simulation-based surgical training. It "integrates principles of curriculum development and simulation design" and involves best practices such as individualized learning, formative and summative feedback, deliberate practice with formative feedback, and mastery learning progressing from novice, competent, proficient, expert to master. The article recommends it alongside proficiency and progression-based simulator training with quantitative performance metrics.
requirements: Measurable quantitative criteria for technical performance
Progression through defined proficiency levels from novice to master
target_learners: surgical trainees progressing from novice to master
examples: The article cites the model's best practices including deliberate practice with formative feedback and mastery learning stages
key_sources: Hedman Leif Rune, Felländer-Tsai Li. (2020). Simulation-based skills training in non-performing orthopedic surgeons: skills acquisition, motivation, and flow during the COVID-19 pandemic. Acta Orthopaedica. https://doi.org/10.1080/17453674.2020.1781413
